tldr: Chain-of-Verification (CoVe): draft an answer, plan verification questions about its factual claims, answer those questions without the draft in context, then regenerate. Wikidata list precision 0.17 -> 0.36 and biography FactScore 55.9 -> 71.4, with no tools or retraining.
method: Four prompted steps on one frozen base LLM (Llama 65B, 3 few-shot examples, greedy decoding): (1) generate a baseline response; (2) plan verification questions covering the draft's factual claims, freely phrased by the model rather than templated; (3) execute those verifications; (4) generate the final verified response conditioned on the question-answer pairs. Step 3 has four variants differing in what may attend to what: joint (plan and answer in one prompt, so answers still see the draft), 2-step (questions answered with the draft removed from context), factored (each question answered in its own prompt, so no draft and no cross-question interference, and prompts batch in parallel), and factor+revise (adds one cross-check prompt per question emitting CONSISTENT / INCONSISTENT / PARTIALLY CONSISTENT). The final prompt presents the verification answers as coming from "another source".
results: Wikidata list questions (micro precision, Llama 65B few-shot): 0.17 -> 0.36 with 2-step CoVe, driven by hallucinations collapsing (negatives 2.95 -> 0.68) while correct entities dip only slightly (0.59 -> 0.38).
Harder Wiki-Category list task: precision 0.12 -> 0.22 with factored CoVe (negatives 4.05 -> 1.52); factored beats joint on every task.
Closed-book MultiSpanQA: F1 0.39 -> 0.48 (factored), a 23% gain from both precision (0.40 -> 0.50) and recall (0.38 -> 0.46).

Biography generation (FactScore, Min et al. metric): 55.9 -> 71.4 with factor+revise, +28%, at 16.6 -> 12.3 average facts; this beats ChatGPT 58.7 and retrieval-augmented PerplexityAI 61.6 using only the base model (joint 60.8, factored 63.7).

Diagnostics: only ~17% of the few-shot baseline's list entities are correct, yet ~70% of those same facts are answered correctly when queried individually; question form matters (Table 4, Wiki-Category) - LLM-written open questions (factored 0.22) beat yes/no (0.19) and templated rule-based (0.16); and neither instruction tuning nor CoT helps (Llama 2 70B Chat zero-shot F1 0.20 vs few-shot Llama 65B 0.39).
advantages: Reduces hallucination with no retrieval, no tools and no weight updates - purely inference-time deliberation on a frozen model - yet still out-fact-scores ChatGPT and a retrieval-augmented system on biographies.

Isolates attention control as the causal mechanism rather than crediting 'more compute': joint < 2-step < factored across tasks shows the gain comes from stopping verification from attending to the hallucinated draft, and Table 4 shows generated questions beat templated heuristics.

Is not precision bought with recall: hallucinated entities fall 2.95 -> 0.68 while correct ones only dip 0.59 -> 0.38, and since FactScore is normalized, producing fewer facts is not the explanation (clipping Llama 2 to 10 sentences only moved 41.3 -> 42.7).

Supplies the reusable design pattern for self-checking - decompose the check into short, independently answerable questions and keep each one blind to the text being checked - which later verification and memory-evolution loops inherit.
limitations: CoVe does not remove hallucinations, only reduces them; the paper's own Section 6 concedes it can still produce incorrect or misleading output.
Scope is directly stated factual inaccuracies (and, on Wikidata/Wiki-Category, listed entities) - not errors inside reasoning steps and not opinions.

The ceiling is the base model's own knowledge, since verification is performed by the same weights: Figure 2 shows retrieval-augmented PerplexityAI still wins on very rare facts, and the paper names tool use as the obvious extension.
Extra cost: more generated tokens, like chain-of-thought, and factored CoVe runs many more prompts (batchable, but no cost analysis or variance/error bars are reported across the four tasks).
fits: Stage 3, self-verification - the positive counterpart to the stage's negative result. CoVe works where intrinsic self-correction fails because verification is decomposed into short, independent, more-answerable questions instead of asking the model to judge its own reasoning. Pairs with Self-Refine (the loop it disagrees with), CRITIC (the tool-grounded version of step 3) and Self-Consistency.
reading: Section 3 for the four steps and the joint / 2-step / factored / factor+revise variants; Tables 1-3 for the numbers; Table 4 and Section 9 with Section 6 for question form and limits.
